h1:
Ploenchit Half-Day Plan
Garden, Thai-Style Church, Embassy Row
intro: This plan is built for anyone with half a day in Ploenchit – Wireless Rd who wants a French cafe in a green garden, a century-old teak house, a Michelin-listed lunch, a Thai-style church unlike anywhere else in the city, a shaded embassy street, and a chocolate cafe tucked into a quiet soi to close it out. Almost the whole route is walkable, with just one short Grab hop along the way. It suits anyone staying nearby, history and photography-minded visitors, or anyone who wants to see a side of Bangkok that isn't just malls.
chips: ☕ Start the morning inside Nai Lert Park
🏛️ A teak house over 100 years old
🍫 Close out with a chocolate cafe in Ruamrudee
quickAnswerHtml: A half-day Ploenchit-Wireless Road itinerary in Bangkok: start at 10am with coffee at École Ducasse – Nai Lert Bangkok Café, tour the Nai Lert Park Heritage Home and Chao Mae Tuptim Shrine, eat a French lunch at Ma Maison, stop by Holy Redeemer Church, walk the leafy Embassy Row on Wireless Road, then finish at 4pm at the chocolate cafe Tempered — all walkable from BTS Ploen Chit, with opening hours and distances for each stop.

blocks.html: Ploenchit – Wireless Rd is a neighborhood where old and new sit unusually close together. A short walk from BTS Ploenchit drops you straight into Nai Lert Park, hiding a century-old teak house, while Wireless Road and Ruamrudee Soi just beyond are thick with embassies and international restaurants. Here's a route we've actually mapped out — starting with morning coffee in the garden, moving through the old house, a Michelin-listed lunch, a Thai-style church, embassy row, and finishing at a chocolate cafe tucked into a quiet lane. Every stop here is a real place people in this neighborhood recommend to each other.

blocks.label: Half-day
blocks.title: Morning to afternoon — French cafe, Nai Lert Park Heritage Home, a Michelin-listed lunch, a Thai-style church, Embassy Row, a chocolate cafe

items.activity: Morning coffee at École Ducasse – Nai Lert Bangkok Café
items.note: Start the day in the garden at École Ducasse – Nai Lert Bangkok Café, the French café run by chef Alain Ducasse's cooking studio inside Nai Lert Park on Soi Somkid. Order the Tarte aux Fraises, the house signature strawberry tart, with a Dirty coffee, and sit looking out at the green lawn before the trip begins. It's open daily roughly 07:00–18:00.

items.activity: Tour Nai Lert Park Heritage Home and the Chao Mae Tuptim Shrine
items.note: Walk within the same garden to Nai Lert Park Heritage Home, a teak house more than 100 years old that belonged to the Nai Lert family. Visits run in guided rounds, with adult admission around 350 THB. Along the way, stop to pay respects at the Chao Mae Tuptim Shrine, the palad khik shrine now relocated into the same grounds. It's open Wednesday to Sunday roughly 09:30–16:30, closed Monday and Tuesday.

Walk a few steps further into Nai Lert Park to Ma Maison, a Thai restaurant serving Khunying Sin's family recipes that has earned a Michelin Guide listing. Order the signature Nai Lert Park noodle soup with steamed fish curry, and sit in the glass pavilion looking out over the lawn. Expect to spend around 600–1,400 baht a head; it's open 11:00–14:30 and 18:00–22:00.

Walk or take a short Grab from Nai Lert Park to Ruamrudee Soi, about 10–15 minutes, to reach Holy Redeemer Church, a Catholic church built in a stacked Thai-temple roof style you won't find anywhere else in the city. Entry is free; dress modestly. It's open daily 06:30–19:00.

Continue on foot to Wireless Road, home to the most densely packed cluster of embassies in Thailand — more than 19 of them — shaded by century-old rain trees. It's free to walk, and the roughly 2-kilometer stretch leads up to Central Embassy at the top of the road; a relaxed walk takes under an hour if you don't linger too long.

items.activity: Close out at Tempered, a chocolate cafe
items.note: Before heading back, stop at Tempered, one of Thailand's first bean-to-bar cocoa roasters, tucked into Soi Ruamrudee 2. Order the single-origin chocolate made from Phattalung cocoa beans with an almond croissant, and rest your feet before walking back to BTS Ploenchit. It's open daily 08:00–18:00.

blocks.title: A timing trick so the days line up
blocks.html: Nai Lert Park Heritage Home is closed Monday and Tuesday, so avoid those two days if you want to tour the teak house. As for getting back, BTS Ploenchit sits directly on the Sukhumvit line, so you can ride straight to Siam or over toward Asok–Ekkamai without changing trains. If you're heading to Suvarnabhumi Airport, connect to the Airport Rail Link at Makkasan station, which isn't far from this neighborhood.

blocks.text: Adjust the plan to your time and style

blocks.html: Ploenchit and Wireless Road is the embassy-and-old-houses quarter, quieter than the mall belt next door. Its appeal is shade and architecture, so shape the plan around what interests you.

items: Only three hours: keep Nai Lert Park Heritage Home → lunch at Ma Maison → the Wireless Road walk. History, a proper meal and the embassy-district atmosphere in one line.
Here for architecture and history: give the heritage home more time — it holds the Nai Lert family's collection and story — then add Holy Redeemer Church, a rare Thai-style Catholic church.

With kids: this district involves a lot of open-air walking and has no dedicated play stop. With small children, cut the Wireless Road stretch and shift to neighbouring Central Embassy or Central Chidlom.
Shooting photos: late afternoon light suits both the heritage home and Wireless Road, so start at midday instead and finish at Tempered in the early evening.

blocks.title: Know before you go: Ploenchit-Wireless Road

items.title: Start at Ploen Chit and walk
items.text: BTS Ploen Chit is the best base — the heritage home and Wireless Road are a few hundred metres away, and a skywalk carries you onward to Chidlom.

items.title: Budget per person
items.text: Around 800-1,500 baht. The heritage home charges admission, while Holy Redeemer Church and the Wireless Road walk are free. Check the ticket price and tour times in advance.

items.title: Check opening days first
items.text: Unlike the malls, the heritage home and several restaurants here close one day a week. Confirm before you set out so the trip is not wasted.

items.title: If it rains
items.text: Wireless Road is shaded but not covered. When it rains, move to Central Embassy via the skywalk and come back to the walk once it eases.

faq.q: Where's the best place to start this Ploenchit half-day plan?
faq.a: Start in Nai Lert Park near BTS Ploenchit or Chit Lom, since the morning coffee, Nai Lert Park Heritage Home and lunch are all in the same garden, before you walk over to the Wireless Road – Ruamrudee area in the afternoon.

faq.q: Do I need to book anything in advance?
faq.a: Nai Lert Park Heritage Home runs guided tours in scheduled rounds, so check the page or call ahead since it sometimes closes for private events. For Ma Maison, book a table in advance if you're going for lunch on a weekend.

faq.q: Which days should I avoid for this plan?
faq.a: Avoid Monday and Tuesday if you want to tour Nai Lert Park Heritage Home, since it's closed those two days. Every other stop on the route keeps its normal hours daily.

faq.q: How do I visit the Nai Lert Park Heritage Home?
faq.a: It is a house museum with paid admission and scheduled viewing slots. Check opening hours and its weekly closing day in advance, as it does not open daily the way mall attractions do.

faq.q: How does this area differ from Chidlom next door?
faq.a: Chidlom is the busy mall-and-shrine belt. Ploenchit and Wireless Road are much quieter — embassies, old houses and mature trees — better suited to a slow walk than to shopping.
